title: Can You Score 80% On This Car Mechanic Quiz?
summary: Read dashboard clues, explore car systems and solve workshop puzzles across five different rounds.

landing.intro:
Know your way around a car?
Put your skills to the test.

about.body:
Five rounds. Five ways to test your car knowledge. Read dashboard clues, explore how parts work, reason through supplied measurements, separate facts from myths and finish with short fault-finding scenarios.

There are six text-only questions per round. Choose one of four answers to move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. Your target is 24 correct answers out of 30.

The questions use general vehicle principles, not country-specific road rules or inspection standards. Vehicle types, units and any example limits are stated where needed. A likely cause is a starting point for diagnosis, not proof that a part needs replacing.

steps: Press Start Quiz, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question. Each round changes the challenge, and questions advance automatically.
Complete all five rounds to reveal your score. You can then unlock your system breakdown and missed-answer review.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This quiz is not a professional qualification or vehicle-repair diagnosis. Vehicles differ; consult the manufacturer’s guidance and a qualified technician.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your first six answers are in. Now discover what happens behind those warning lights.

next.tagline: Match each part to its job.

stage-2.preAdCopy: Two rounds complete. Next, use the numbers and clues supplied.

next.tagline: Read the evidence. Work out the answer.

stage-3.preAdCopy: You have worked through the readings. Can you separate sound advice from common myths?

next.tagline: One accurate statement. Three wrong turns.

stage-4.preAdCopy: One round left. Follow the clues without jumping to conclusions.

next.tagline: Six scenarios. Choose the strongest next step.

stage-5.preAdCopy: All 30 answers are in. Reveal your score and discover your strongest vehicle system.

profile-1.title: The Workshop Quiz Expert
profile-1.copy: You connected parts, measurements and diagnostic clues with excellent accuracy on this quiz. Your review shows how you handled each vehicle system.

profile-2.title: The Workshop Natural
profile-2.copy: You read warning signs confidently and understood how the major vehicle systems work together. Your diagnostic instincts stayed reliable as the jobs became more demanding.

profile-3.title: The Skilled Fault Finder
profile-3.copy: You followed most of the clues and handled a broad mix of vehicle systems well. Review the answers you missed to see where a closer look would help.

profile-4.title: The Practical Problem-Solver
profile-4.copy: You have a useful map of everyday vehicle systems and a sensible approach to diagnosis. Your strongest rounds show where your hands-on knowledge really clicks.

profile-5.title: The Hands-On Learner
profile-5.copy: You identified a solid share of the workshop faults across very different systems. Some clues were familiar immediately, while others are ready for another look.

profile-6.title: The Curious Car Owner
profile-6.copy: The Service Bay uncovered some knowledge gaps, but it also showed where your automotive instincts are strongest. Every missed fault is another useful clue to learn.

score.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This score is not a professional qualification, a vehicle safety inspection or repair advice.

mechanic-r1q1.question: An oil-can warning light is commonly associated with which engine problem?

mechanic-r1q2.question: What does ABS stand for on a car dashboard?

mechanic-r1q3.question: In a conventional fuel-powered car, a battery-shaped warning stays on while the engine runs. Which system needs checking?

mechanic-r1q4.question: A thermometer symbol above wavy lines commonly warns about what?

mechanic-r1q5.question: A dashboard message says “Power steering assist fault.” Which task may become harder?

mechanic-r1q6.question: Some warning lights turn on briefly at startup, then go out as the manual describes. What can this be?

answers.a1: A normal system or lamp check
answers.a2: Proof that every system is fault-free
answers.a3: A reminder to replace every sensor
answers.a4: A sign that the lights are disconnected

mechanic-r2q1.question: What is the main job of an engine air filter?

answers.a3: Trap particles before air enters the engine

mechanic-r2q2.question: In a disc brake, what do the brake pads press against to slow the wheel?

mechanic-r2q3.question: In a conventional car with a running engine, what is the alternator mainly doing?

answers.a1: Turning the engine before it starts
answers.a4: Supplying electrical power and charging the battery

mechanic-r2q4.question: What does a thermostat normally regulate in an engine cooling system?

answers.a2: Coolant flow to help control engine temperature

mechanic-r2q5.question: Why does a conventional differential allow the driven wheels to turn at different speeds?

answers.a1: They must always turn in opposite directions
answers.a2: One wheel must stop whenever the car turns
answers.a3: They travel different distances when cornering
answers.a4: It prevents all wheel slip on every surface

mechanic-r2q6.question: Which tool is designed to tighten a fastener to a specified torque?

mechanic-r3q1.question: A test car uses 18 L of fuel over 300 km. At the same rate, how much would it use over 100 km?

mechanic-r3q2.question: A test car specifies 220 kPa for all four cold tires. Readings are 220, 220, 180 and 220 kPa. Which reading is below the stated target?

mechanic-r3q3.question: Two identical lamps share a power supply. One works and one does not. Which conclusion is supported by that fact alone?

answers.a1: The unlit bulb must be broken
answers.a2: The supply is not completely dead
answers.a4: The working lamp has a short circuit

mechanic-r3q4.question: A training example needs 4 L of a mixture containing 50% coolant concentrate by volume. How much concentrate is that?

mechanic-r3q5.question: A gearbox has a 3:1 reduction ratio. If the input turns at 1,200 rpm, what is the output speed?

mechanic-r3q6.question: The stated minimum thickness for a test component is 3.0 mm. It measures 2.5 mm. What does the measurement establish?

answers.a2: It is below the stated minimum
answers.a3: The measuring tool must be faulty
answers.a4: The component is exactly new thickness

mechanic-r4q1.question: Which statement about engine oil is accurate?

answers.a1: Thicker oil is best for every engine
answers.a2: All oils with the same colour are identical
answers.a3: Oil never needs changing if its level stays full
answers.a4: The specified grade matters; thicker is not always better

mechanic-r4q2.question: Which statement about ABS is accurate?

answers.a1: It guarantees the shortest stop on every surface
answers.a2: It helps prevent wheel lock but cannot guarantee a shorter stop on every surface
answers.a3: It replaces the need for tire grip
answers.a4: It makes worn brake pads work like new ones

mechanic-r4q3.question: Which statement about electric cars is accurate?

answers.a1: All electrical parts connect directly to the main drive battery
answers.a2: Electric cars cannot have low-voltage battery faults
answers.a3: Many have a separate low-voltage battery as well as the main drive battery
answers.a4: A charged drive battery proves every electrical system is healthy

mechanic-r4q4.question: Which is the reliable way to choose a compatible engine coolant?

answers.a1: Follow the vehicle manufacturer’s coolant specification
answers.a2: Match its colour and ignore the specification
answers.a4: Assume all products marked coolant are interchangeable

mechanic-r4q5.question: Which statement separates wheel balancing from wheel alignment?

answers.a1: Both are names for the same adjustment
answers.a2: Balancing changes wheel angles; alignment adds wheel weights
answers.a3: Neither can affect how the car feels on the road
answers.a4: Balancing corrects weight imbalance; alignment adjusts wheel angles

mechanic-r4q6.question: A diagnostic scan reports a sensor-circuit fault. What does that establish?

answers.a1: The sensor must always be replaced
answers.a2: The wiring has already passed every test
answers.a3: The circuit needs diagnosis; the sensor is not automatically the cause
answers.a4: Clearing the code permanently repairs the fault

mechanic-r5q1.question: A trained technician moves an ignition coil to another cylinder during diagnosis. The misfire moves with it. Which suspect does this most strongly support?

mechanic-r5q2.question: A car suddenly pulls strongly to one side when braking. What is the safest next step?

answers.a1: Stop safely and arrange a professional inspection
answers.a2: Keep driving until the pull disappears
answers.a3: Use higher speed to compare the braking
answers.a4: Assume it is harmless if no warning light appears

mechanic-r5q3.question: A new battery repeatedly loses charge, and the charging warning appears while the engine runs. What should be investigated?

answers.a1: Only the age of the new battery
answers.a3: The charging system and its connections

mechanic-r5q4.question: An engine overheats at idle but cools at road speed. During a technician’s test, the cooling fan is commanded on but does not run. What should be checked first?

answers.a2: The fan motor, power supply and control circuit

mechanic-r5q5.question: A steering-wheel vibration is strongest within one road-speed range. Which is a sensible early check, not a confirmed diagnosis?

answers.a4: Wheel and tire condition and balance

mechanic-r5q6.question: A car is supported only by a portable jack. Someone is about to work underneath it. What is the safe decision?

answers.a1: Do not go underneath until it is correctly supported with suitable equipment
answers.a2: Go underneath if the job will take less than a minute
answers.a3: Go underneath if the engine is switched off
answers.a4: Go underneath if another person holds the jack handle
